title: Finance Assistant - 12 Month Contract
description:
Job Title: Finance Assistant - Maternity Cover (Fixed Term Contract)
Salary: 29,000 - 31,000 per annum
Location: LS7, Parking on site
Contract Length: 12 months, Hybrid available (minimum of 2-3 days in the office)
Working Pattern: Full-Time (37.5 hours per week)

Our client, a reputable charity, is seeking a dedicated Finance Assistant to join their team for a maternity cover position. This is an exciting opportunity for an individual who thrives in a fast-paced environment and is eager to contribute to day-to-day financial operations while supporting the Finance Director and other team members.

Main Purpose of the Job:
The Finance Assistant will be responsible for managing daily financial matters, ensuring adherence to financial policies and procedures, and maintaining proper financial control over the organisation's income, assets, and liabilities.

Key Responsibilities:
- Process daily bank transactions through automatic bank feeds into QuickBooks
- Conduct monthly bank reconciliations to ensure accuracy
- Handle supplier invoices and prepare weekly payment runs with precision
- Manage staff expense claims and ensure timely processing
- Oversee donation processing and maintain updated donation analysis
- Take charge of Rent Cards, including processing housing benefit payments and liaising with relevant staff on rental income and tenant debtors
- Maintain recurring invoice templates in QuickBooks and allocate payments accordingly
- Process month-end journals, including prepayments and accruals
- Produce and issue the Monthly Management Accounts pack along with departmental Cost Control Reports
- Support the Finance Director during the annual audit and undertake other ad hoc duties as required

Essential Skills & Experience:
- Relevant finance experience in a similar role.
- Proficiency in maintaining robust financial accounting and software systems.
- Excellent attention to detail and strong problem-solving capabilities.
- Ability to prioritise and manage a varied workload effectively.
- Strong interpersonal and communication skills, particularly in cross-team collaboration.
- IT literacy, particularly advanced skills in Microsoft Office and experience with Excel.

Education & Training:
- AAT qualification or equivalent experience is preferred.

Why Consider This Role?
This is a fantastic opportunity for a finance professional looking to make a meaningful impact while gaining exposure to various aspects of financial management within a supportive environment. The role offers a competitive salary, the chance to work closely with senior management, and the ability to contribute to the organisation's financial success.

If you are ready to take on this exciting challenge and bring your financial expertise to our client, please apply today! Your skills could make a significant difference in this vibrant organisation.

Scan patient-related documents onto their medical record using read codes as agreed by the clinical team Add any additional information about the source of the document Forward the document to the doctor or nurse who initiated the referral or who is most appropriate to receive the information Ensure incoming letters are scanned onto the patient record within a 48/72-hour timescale Scan all internal paper documents on to the relevant patients record and then store the documents in line with surgery procedures. Coding Identify relevant clinical information contained in patient correspondence Code or free text the clinical information on to the patient record Deal with queries relating to coding Appointments Process appointment requests for today and future appointments from patients by telephone and in person. Deal with visit requests and produce any documentation required for the doctors. Arrange and record hospital transport requests. Computer Carry out data input, ensuring that the recording of all relevant information into the patients electronic medical record is accurate and concise. Registration of new patients computer data entry and medical records. Process patients change of address computer data and medical records. Process applications from patients for online Patient Access. Process repeat prescription requests in accordance with practice guidelines. Telephone Have working knowledge of telephone system, during and after hours. Other Tasks Ensure building security have thorough knowledge of doors/windows/alarm. Open up premises at the start of the day if the first to arrive and make all necessary preparations to receive patients. Make refreshments (tea/coffee) for doctors and colleagues. Any other tasks allocated by the Partners or Practice Manager. In the performance of the duties outlined in this Job Description, the post-holder may have access to confidential information relating to patients and their carers, practice staff and other healthcare workers. They may also have access to information relating to the practice as a business organisation. All such information from any source is to be regarded as strictly confidential. Information relating to patients, carers, colleagues, other healthcare workers or the business of the practice may only be divulged to authorised persons in accordance with the practice policies and procedures relating to confidentiality and the protection of personal and sensitive data. Health & Safety : The post-holder will assist in promoting and maintaining their own and others health, safety and security as defined in the practice Health & Safety Policy, to include: Using personal security systems within the workplace according to practice guidelines. Identifying the risks involved in work activities and undertaking such activities in a way that manages those risks. Making effective use of training to update knowledge and skills. Using appropriate infection control procedures, maintaining work areas in a tidy and safe way and free from hazards. Reporting potential risks identified. Personal/professional development: The post-holder will participate in any training programme implemented by the practice as part of this employment, such training to include: Participation in an annual individual performance review, including taking responsibility for maintaining a record of own personal and/or professional development Taking responsibility for own development, learning and performance and demonstrating skills and activities to others who are undertaking similar work Equality and Diversity : The post-holder will support the equality, diversity and rights of patients, carers and colleagues, to include: Acting in a way that recognizes the importance of peoples rights, interpreting them in a way that is consistent with practice procedures and policies, and current legislation. Taking responsibility for own development, learning and performance and demonstrating skills and activities to others who are undertaking similar work. Assess own performance and take accountability for own actions, either directly or under supervision. Contribute to the effectiveness of the team by reflecting on own and team activities and making suggestions on ways to improve and enhance the teams performance. Work effectively with individuals in other agencies to meet patients needs. Effectively manage own time, workload and resources. Communication : The post-holder should recognise the importance of effective communication within the team and will strive to: Communicate effectively with other team members, patients and carers. Recognise peoples needs for alternative methods of communication and respond accordingly. Contribution to the Implementation of Services : The post-holder will: Work in accordance with practice policies, standards and guidance. Discuss with other members of the team how the policies, standards and guidelines will affect own work. Make use of information technology systems available within the Practice, following systems for data security and protection. Participate in audit where appropriate. Attend and participate in practice meetings/training events. Any other duties commensurate with the role to ensure the smooth running of the Practice. title: Medical Receptionist
description: A new opportunity has arisen for a medical receptionist to join our team. The vacancy is part time, working 20 hours per week Monday 08:00 - 13:00 Thursday 08:00 - 14:00 Friday 08:30 - 18:30 Receptionists are the first line of contact with our patients. This is a varied role that includes face to face and telephone contact with patients as well as administrative duties. It requires a high level of attention to detail to ensure an excellent service is provided to both our patients and the clinical and non-clinical staff at the practice. Job Title: Medical Receptionist Location: Harrogate Road or Harehills Community Health Centre Hours per week: 20 Hours per week Reports to : Reception Supervisor DBS Check: Enhanced Check Job Summary Duties and responsibilities: Maintaining and monitoring the practice appointments system; Processing personal and telephone requests for appointments, visits and telephone consultations, and ensuring callers are directed to the appropriate healthcare professional Processing and distributing incoming (and outgoing) mail Dealing with enquiries via email. Taking messages and passing on information for clinical and non-clinical staff Filing and retrieving paperwork, recording and receipting of petty cash. Processing repeat prescriptions in accordance with practice guidelines. Processing, all repeat medication requests sent in by patients using the various protocols in place. Collecting repeat prescription requests from post box and reception. Liaising with patients and chemists regarding queries and requests Ensuring repeat medication is issued in line with the protocols that are already in place, and ensure that any queries raised are dealt with quickly and correctly. Ensuring that patient queries on medication are highlighted to the relevant GP. Regularly go through prescriptions not picked up and unlikely to be picked up as a result of the timescale, to remove the details from the patient records and then destroy the prescription. Initiating contact with and responding to requests from patients, other team member and associated healthcare agencies and providers Ensuring incoming colleagues are fully briefed on any urgent or unresolved issues. title: Care Navigator/ Medical Receptionist
description: South Queen Street Medical Centre are looking to appoint a care navigator/ receptionist to join our busy GP practice who will be the first point of contact for patients, contractors, and visitors as well as carrying out general office management tasks. Working pattern 5 hours per day, 5 days a week, alternate weekly am & pm shifts, 8am-630pm. Flexibility and overtime will be required for this role. You will be responsible for the general reception duties within the Practice and work with our established processes, policies, and procedures to provide a comprehensive high-quality service and deal efficiently and courteously with patient enquiries. You will receive, assist, and direct patients in accessing the appropriate service or healthcare professional in a courteous, efficient and effective way. You will provide general assistance to the practice team and project a positive and friendly image to patients and other visitors, either in person or via the telephone. You will have excellent communication skills, a compassionate and friendly nature who can operate in a busy environment with a range of people and professions, as you will be working with our clinical and administration teams. This role is ideal for someone who is highly organised and an effective communicator who can provide a professional and warm welcome to our patients, ensuring every contact is of the highest quality. IT skills are essential, as you will be regularly creating searches, data input and monitoring our achievements and progress against national, local, and internal targets. You will also process prescription requests and provide a full administrative service. GCSE grade C or above in English and Maths is essential for this role. Key Duties and Responsibilities Patient Reception and Customer Service Act as the first point of contact for patients, visitors and healthcare professionals, both face-to-face and over the telephone. Welcome patients in a friendly, respectful and professional manner. Respond to general enquiries and provide accurate information about practice services, opening hours and appointment procedures. Deal sensitively with patients who may be anxious, distressed, frustrated or experiencing difficult personal circumstances. Maintain a clean, organised and welcoming reception and waiting area. Manage challenging situations professionally and escalate complaints or concerns to the appropriate member of the practice team. Care Navigation and Appointment Management Handle patient requests for appointments, advice and access to healthcare services by telephone and in person. Use approved care navigation protocols to direct patients to the most appropriate clinician or service, including GPs, practice nurses, clinical pharmacists, physiotherapists and other available services where appropriate. Gather relevant non-clinical information to help determine the appropriate appointment pathway, without attempting to diagnose medical conditions. Book, amend and cancel appointments using the practices clinical computer system. Identify potentially urgent concerns in accordance with practice procedures and promptly escalate them to a clinician. Provide information about alternative services, such as NHS 111, where appropriate and in accordance with practice guidance. Maintain accurate records of patient contacts and appointment requests. Telephone and Administrative Duties Answer incoming telephone calls promptly and manage a busy call queue efficiently. Handle patient messages and ensure they are passed to the appropriate member of the clinical or administrative team. Process repeat prescription requests in accordance with practice policies and direct medication queries to the appropriate professional. Register new patients and update demographic details, contact information and other relevant records. Manage incoming and outgoing post, emails and electronic communications. Assist with administrative tasks, including recalling patients for appointments, supporting clinical audits and maintaining accurate practice records. Monitor outstanding administrative tasks and follow up requests within agreed timescales. Clinical Systems and Data Management Use the practices electronic clinical system, SystmOne, to access and update patient information. Ensure patient details, appointment information and messages are recorded accurately and promptly. Handle sensitive patient information securely and maintain strict confidentiality at all times. Comply with UK GDPR, data protection legislation, information governance requirements and practice policies. Follow procedures for accessing, storing and sharing patient information appropriately. Teamwork and Practice Support Work collaboratively with GPs, nurses, healthcare assistants, pharmacists, care coordinators and administrative colleagues. Attend staff meetings and training sessions as required. Support colleagues during busy periods and assist with the day-to-day organisation of reception services. Follow practice policies relating to health and safety, infection prevention, safeguarding and equality and diversity. Report incidents, risks and concerns to the appropriate manager. Undertake other reasonable duties appropriate to the role to support the effective operation of the practice. Training and Development The successful candidate will receive induction and training appropriate to the role, including practice procedures, clinical systems, information governance, confidentiality, safeguarding, health and safety and care navigation. Ongoing training and development will be encouraged to support the delivery of a safe, efficient and high-quality patient service. Personal Qualities We are looking for someone who is approachable, empathetic, dependable and proactive. The successful candidate must demonstrate patience, discretion and professionalism when dealing with sensitive situations and be committed to treating every patient with dignity, respect and fairness. Working Conditions The postholder will work within a busy GP practice and may be required to work flexibly according to the needs of the service. Working hours, salary, annual leave and other employment terms will be confirmed during recruitment.

title: Medical Receptionist
description: Kensington Partnership is seeking a friendly, professional and organised Medical Receptionist to join our busy GP practice team. The successful candidate will provide efficient reception and administrative support, ensuring patients receive a welcoming and professional service. Excellent communication, IT and organisational skills are essential, along with the ability to work under pressure, use initiative and work effectively as part of a team. Previous NHS, GP reception or SystmOne experience is desirable, but full training will be provided. Flexibility to cover staff absences and work across practice sites where required is also desirable. Recruitment Process Shortlisted candidates will be invited to a pre-interview information session on Thursday, 19 November 2026, from 1:00 pm to 3:00 pm , to gain a better understanding of the role and its expectations. Those who remain interested will be invited to a formal interview at a later date. You will join a supportive, forward-thinking team, delivering professional and compassionate patient services within a busy primary care environment. With most incoming calls managed through our AI system, the role primarily involves handling face-to-face enquiries, supporting AI-assisted triage and providing administrative support. Responsibilities include reviewing and processing patient requests, maintaining accurate records, directing enquiries to appropriate teams and escalating clinical concerns in accordance with practice procedures. Occasional telephone duties may also be required. A courteous, confidential and patient-centred approach is essential at all times. Reception and Patient Services Welcome patients and manage face-to-face enquiries professionally and courteously. Handle calls transferred by the AI telephone system requiring receptionist assistance. Support AI-assisted triage by reviewing and processing patient requests in line with practice procedures. Book appointments following triage outcomes and provide appropriate care navigation. Signpost patients to relevant services and escalate urgent or complex concerns to the clinical team. Administration and Practice Support Maintain accurate patient records using SystmOne and other practice systems. Process correspondence, home visit requests, ambulance transport and interpreter bookings. Handle payments, receipts, deliveries and general administrative duties. Provide day-to-day administrative support to GPs, clinical staff and colleagues. Communication and Teamwork Communicate professionally and compassionately with patients, carers, colleagues and external agencies. Work collaboratively and flexibly across practice sites as required. Support patients with additional communication or accessibility needs. Undertake chaperone duties when appropriately trained and authorised. Confidentiality and Information Governance Maintain strict confidentiality and access patient records only when authorised and necessary. Comply with UK GDPR, the Data Protection Act 2018 and practice information governance policies. Promptly report suspected data breaches, security incidents or confidentiality concerns. General Responsibilities Assist with opening and securing practice premises when authorised. Maintain a safe, tidy and welcoming reception environment. Follow safeguarding, infection prevention, health and safety, and other practice policies. Complete mandatory training and undertake other reasonable duties appropriate to the role.
